records.title: Archivarius
records.purpose: One validated JSON file - a snapshot - holds a project's whole description as small linked records: its parts, the rules they must satisfy, the decisions behind them, the work left and the checks that confirm it. A React library draws that file as an architecture map that reveals more detail as it is zoomed.

records.title: Purpose of the library
records.statement: An owner understands a system's structure, the grounds for decisions, the remaining work and the effect of changes from one snapshot; an LLM reads and edits the same records.

records.title: The repository describes itself
records.statement: The snapshot in this repository describes Archivarius itself, so the map below, the tables under it and this page are the project's own records drawn by the library it documents.

records.title: Provenance and freshness model
records.statement: A record keeps the definitions it was written against apart from the records it merely mentions, so when a definition changes, whatever rested on it stops counting as confirmed instead of quietly staying green.

records.title: Model and contract
records.summary: Owns the v4 JSON schema, record types, graph references, history, snapshots and the validated-change contract.

records.title: Core
records.summary: Parses and validates a model, projects a v4 project to an architecture, and analyzes freshness and completion.
records.boundary: Layout and rendering stay outside the core.

records.title: Graph references
records.summary: Validates typed relations between records and reports reverse links and coverage.
records.boundary: Reference semantics are fixed by the schema targets.

records.title: Canonical digest
records.summary: Computes the SHA-256 basis over a canonical representation of the definitions.
records.boundary: The canonicalization rules are internal to the digest.

records.title: Node API
records.summary: Reads a model file, verifies evidence artifacts by bytes, applies validated changes, and generates documentation.

records.title: CLI
records.summary: Exposes validate, read, context, apply, reference, readme, documents, verify, run and archive over the model file.
records.boundary: Argument parsing and file paths stay inside the CLI.

records.title: Evidence verification
records.summary: Matches declared binding bytes against files and records actual check outcomes.
records.boundary: Executing checks is performed by the run command, not by loading a model.

records.title: Map rendering
records.summary: Mounts an interactive architecture map with semantic zoom and an inspector for records.

records.title: Architecture map
records.summary: Lays out components and interactions and reveals detail as the map is zoomed.
records.boundary: Layout geometry stays inside the map.

records.title: Inspector and overview
records.summary: Shows a record's meaning, links, implementation outcome and the reasons requiring attention.
records.boundary: Project data and UI copy stay external resources.

records.title: Model source
records.payload: A v4 JSON snapshot as a URL, File, Blob or parsed object.
records.meaning: Any accepted source resolves to one parsed snapshot before anything renders, and a snapshot that fails validation is never partly displayed.

records.title: Change input
records.payload: A context receipt and a change with put and remove sets.
records.meaning: The receipt fixes the definitions the change was written against, so a change computed from definitions that have since moved cannot land.

records.title: Evidence artifact
records.payload: Relative binding paths and the bytes they resolve to.
records.meaning: A declared path confirms only while its bytes still match, so an artifact that was moved or edited stops confirming on the next read.

records.title: Reference set
records.meaning: Every relation resolves to an existing record of a type its field allows, and whatever nothing points at is reported as uncovered.

records.title: Basis value
records.payload: The canonical definitions and their SHA-256 basis.
records.meaning: Equal definitions yield an equal basis whatever their order or edit history, so a differing basis means a definition really changed.

records.title: Record detail
records.payload: A selected record with its links and implementation outcome.
records.meaning: A record arrives with its links and outcome already resolved, so what is shown never depends on a second read of the model.

records.title: One snapshot, one set of definitions
records.rule: Every statement has a single definition; all views render the one selected snapshot.
when: A model is loaded or rendered.

records.title: Views agree with the snapshot
records.assertion: The map, inspector and generated documentation all reflect the same loaded snapshot and definitions.

records.title: Changes are validated against an unchanged context
records.rule: A change requires an unchanged context receipt; a stale context, unknown field or broken reference is rejected and the source file is preserved.
when: A change is applied through the API or CLI.

records.title: Stale or invalid changes are refused
records.assertion: A stale context, unknown field or broken reference is rejected and the input model is left unmodified.

records.title: Confirmation needs byte-exact evidence
records.rule: A check outcome confirms only with an available execution artifact and matching bytes for every declared input; missing or stale evidence does not confirm.

records.title: Stale and missing evidence cannot confirm
records.assertion: A result confirms only when its artifact exists and every declared input's bytes match; otherwise the criterion is not confirmed.

records.title: Conservative freshness
records.rule: Changing any definition conservatively marks dependent decisions, tasks and checks as requiring review; the current review scope is the whole project.

records.title: Dependents are marked for review
records.assertion: After a definition changes, decisions, tasks and checks depending on it report their basis as no longer current.

records.title: Canonical digest for the basis
records.choice: Compute basis.contract as a SHA-256 over a canonical representation of the definitions, excluding results, history and review text.
alternatives: Track freshness by timestamps or manual review flags.
records.because: A content digest detects real definition changes without trusting order or edit metadata.
consequences: Any definition change, including additions, drops the current basis.

records.title: Project data and copy stay external
records.choice: Load model data and UI copy as external resources rather than bundling them into the library.
alternatives: Embed a default model and copy in the shipped scripts.
records.because: The format stays independent of any project, repository or build, and shipped scripts do not carry project data.
consequences: A consumer supplies the model source and container.

records.title: Edit a definition and re-render
steps: Apply a validated change against the unchanged context.
failures: A stale context is rejected and the model is preserved.

records.title: Maintain the model and contract
records.change: Keep the schema, graph references, digest and validated-change path consistent.

records.title: Render the snapshot
records.change: Mount the map and inspector from one loaded snapshot.

records.title: Verify evidence and outcomes
records.change: Match declared binding bytes and record actual check outcomes.

records.title: Model and change validation
records.method: Validate models and reject stale contexts, unknown fields, broken references and forged bases.

records.title: Rendering from one snapshot
records.method: Render the map, inspector and documentation from a single snapshot and confirm they agree.

records.title: Byte-exact evidence
records.method: Confirm outcomes only with an available artifact and matching declared-input bytes.

records.title: One appearance table for every picture
records.choice: Derive how a node and a relation are drawn - tone, shape, outline and line - from one table keyed on the rendering contract's closed enums, and read that table from both the map and the generated diagram; a renderer adds only its own pixels.
alternatives: Style the map in its stylesheet and leave the generated diagram as one flat rectangle per node.
Ship the palette as a consumer-facing asset beside the UI copy.
records.because: A second palette drifts, so the same zone or interaction kind would read differently in the map than in the generated documentation, and a value the contract allows could reach a renderer with no display token at all.
consequences: A value added to a contract enum fails the appearance suite until it is given a token.
Tones belong to the shared vocabulary while dash lengths, stroke widths and radii stay with the surface that draws them.
